utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Good morning, everyone. You may have noticed towards the end of last week that Judge Nosworthy was not very well. Well, she has succumbed, I'm afraid, this morning, and will not be with us today. We have considered the position and decided that it's in the interests of justice that we should continue in her absence meanwhile, and we continue with the evidence of Mr. Filic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Filic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: The examination by Mr. Lukic will continue in a moment. Please bear in mind that the solemn declaration to speak the truth which you made at the beginning of your evidence continues to apply to that evidence today. Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Mr. Filic.

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR FILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: There was something I forgot to ask you previously, hence I will go back to that topic. Do you know of the cases - and please state it briefly - of clashes among Albanians themselves?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR FILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were some mutual clashes between Albanians, in particular Albanians which were doing some sort of business in terms of debts. They seldom reported that to the secretariat. There was a specific case, though, which also had to do with Bozidar Spasic, who was the chief of OUP. He ended up as a victim of kidnapping simply because he lived in the same building with someone who owed some money and resembled that person. A certain entrepreneur from Skopje ordered the kidnapping of a certain Saqir who owed him a few hundred thousand German marks due to certain business transactions. The group that was supposed to kidnap him and transfer him over the Macedonian border, illegally, of course, so that the person who ordered it could retrieve his debts kidnapped Bozidar Spasic, chief of OUP, by mistake. They took him to the area of Kacanik, which is at the border of Macedonia, and they tried to transfer him illegally to Macedonia overnight. They failed because at that time the border was secured more tightly, and in the morning when they realized they had made a mistake they released him.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Let us move on. Briefly again, what regulation did you use based on which you reported to your superiors?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR FILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was done according to the regulation on reporting which prescribed the reporting process in detail.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: What type of reporting was there?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR FILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The instruction envisaged urgent, daily, and periodical reporting. There are cases enumerated in which cases the ministry needs to be advised of certain things urgently by dispatch or phone, and it also prescribes the regular situations as well as monthly and annual reporting circumstances.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: The transcript states instructions. Was it instructions to report, to submit reports?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR FILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, guide-lines.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Were you reporting to the MUP staff and what procedure did you use?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR FILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We reported to them parallelly, daily, as part of daily reporting.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: In what way were you reporting to the MUP staff during the war?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR FILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: During the war, after the Pristina SUP building had been bombed, all special types of communication used by the service was -- were interrupted since the switchboard had been destroyed. It was on the 29th of March. After the 7th of April, when the postal building had been bombed as well, the regular telephone communication was also cut off. All reporting subsequently was done by couriers between the secretariat, then the regional SUP in Pristina, and the ministry.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please have P1092 in e-court.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: The fourth document from the end in your binder. Can you tell us what this notification is about, this dispatch.

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR FILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This dispatch was sent by the department of the police of the SUP in Pristina to all OUPs within its area, deputy chief of the police, Major Vesko Petrovic, signed this. They are asking for more urgent reporting to the chief of the service when circumstances require that. I believe there were some delayed reports sent during the course of the previous period, and this dispatch was urging people to report more promptly.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Was this something that could be considered regular or something that would be not -- that wouldn't be so ordinary?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR FILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This would be a regular way of communicating with the SUP and the OUPs.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. In the secretariats you worked for, were there any RDB employees working there as well?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR FILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: A thing or two about uniforms, please. Can you tell us what sort of uniforms were worn by the police in 1998 and 1999?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR FILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The active-duty and reserve policemen during that time used exclusively camouflage blue uniforms, which they wore in their regular tasks. PJP members had additional green camouflage uniforms with a different hue of the military camouflage green uniform.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: In the SUPs you worked, were there any volunteers?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR FILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the secretariats I worked for were no volunteers. The units were strictly comprised of active-duty and reserve police officers.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: A word or two about the PJP. Within the SUP of Pristina, was there a PJP company?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR FILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were two PJP companies, and I think in B formation there were two as well as in the A formation.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Who commanded those units?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR FILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The companies were commanded by company commanders, and the commander of the 124th Intervention Brigade commanded all PJP members.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: In case that one or two PJP companies of the SUP of Pristina are engaged in combat, what would you be reported on, what sort of reports would you receive?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR FILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The commander of the 124th who was also the chief of the police would advise the chief of the secretariat on the engagement of the PJP in terms of certain tasks. He would also require logistical support, and that would be it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Are you saying the commander of the 124th was the chief of the police department in SUP Pristina?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. His standing appointment was that one according to the establishment. He was the chief of the police department. In addition to that, he commanded the 124th Intervention Brigade.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: The chief of SUP or you as his deputy, would you be reported on any combat activities or actions the PJP participated in?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR FILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The chief of SUP wouldn't have direct contact with a commander during combat, but if there were any casualties, people killed or wounded, PJP members, then he would be notified.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Did you ever plan any actions together with the military, with the Army of Yugoslavia?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR FILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Personally, no, never.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Do you know whether your predecessor at the SUP of Urosevac participated in the action planning together with the VJ?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR FILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Did you ever receive any maps or orders to carry out anti-terrorist actions?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR FILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: What was the relationship between the SAJ and the secretariat of the interior?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR FILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The SAJ was a separate organizational unit of the ministry. They were located in the area of Pristina. For a number of years they had been subordinated directly to the SAJ command in Belgrade, they had their own commander, it was Zivko Trajkovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please have Exhibit 6D618 --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction: 681.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] -- put up in e-court.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Concerning this document, I wanted to ask you whether you knew that there was an engagement of MUP units, or rather, of the PJP outside Kosovo and Metohija?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR FILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I know of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Do you know who decided on the engagement of those units?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR FILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was decided upon by the ministry or the public security sector, as can be seen from the dispatch.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Who sent the dispatch?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR FILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was sent by the public security sector of the Ministry of the Interior to all SUPs from which PJP members are to be taken for this action.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Let us go to the last page, that is, the second page. Is General Djordjevic's name in the signature block?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR FILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, the chief of sector, General Djordjevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: The dispatches of the 28th of July, 1998, so as not to go through all of the documents but similar documents are 6D682 to 6D687. Mr. Filic, did you hear of the spring offensive of the KLA that was supposed to take place in 1999?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR FILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was information in circulation about that. I have no proof, though. Such information existed in the previous years as well throughout the 1990s. Often they had leaflets distributed about the so-called bloody Fridays that were supposed to follow in the following period, but they were just trying to intimidate the population of the province so that the people would start moving out. The same applied to the upcoming spring offensive on the part of the KLA.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We are talking about 1999 this last part of your answer refers to that?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR FILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Did you know that members of the KVM left Kosovo and Metohija; and if so, can you tell us when?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR FILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Members of the KVM left Kosovo and Metohija on the 19th of March, in the evening.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please have Exhibit 6D614 put up in e-court, page 690, item 539. Page 690. We announced -- we notified the Prosecutor of the particular item; however, it was not translated.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us what was the KLA's reaction to the KVM's departure?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR FILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In those days when the KVM left, on the same day and the following few days the KLA transferred its terrorist activities to urban areas. There were terrorist attacks on policemen, police patrols, some bridges were demolished, and so on.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Item 539, what date does it mention and who was killed?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR FILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The 20th of March and it describes the fact that near Luzane in the area of Podujevo a terrorist attack was carried out and policeman Goran Milutinovic was killed, he was from the secretariat of the interior in Belgrade.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Where was he killed?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR FILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the main road, he was ambushed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Item 540, date, place, who was killed?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR FILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: 540 on the 20th of March, 1999, there was an attack on a police patrol --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And what happened?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the witness read more slowly, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] There was an attack, a policeman Goran Milicevic was wounded.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now we need page 691, the last item on page --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Just before you move on to that. Where was Goran Milicevic attacked?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In the village of Drenovac, municipality of Pristina, in a place called Mahala.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: I'm just curious to know that I've understood you correctly. You've said that what happened as the result of KVM withdrawal was that KLA activity transferred to urban areas, but these are not examples of that. Have I heard correctly what you said was the development?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] These cases are being put before me now, but I can tell you cases that occurred in the town of Pristina. On the 21st of March in the town itself in Miladin Popovic Street --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Just a moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we have page 691, item 547.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And, Witness, please continue.

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR FILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In Miladin Popovica Street in the town there was a terrorist attack on a reinforced police patrol of six policemen, and on that occasion four policemen were killed and two were seriously wounded. In the area of Dragodan neighbourhood there was another attack on a police patrol. The patrol responded to the attack, if you open that I'll see the name of the Albanian, I've forgotten his name, he was seriously wounded.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we have the next page, the first paragraph at the top of the page, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: This incident with four policemen, you'd already gone to Dragodan? I don't have Dragodan here among my documents, but if we can look at page 693, item 552. Does this describe an attack in the town and when?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR FILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the 22nd it was reported that a terrorist attack had been carried out in the Medzik cafe in Pristina, Lejonora Jutuli [phoen] was killed and several persons were injured.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we now have P1100.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Mr. Filic, can you see what sort of document this is?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR FILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is a combined daily report of the ministry staff addressed to the Ministry of the Interior of the Republic of Serbia. It's dated the 27th of March, 1999.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And had the air-strikes already begun?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR FILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, three days before that date.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: In item 2, do you see what the consequences of the terrorist attacks were?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR FILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Item 2, if we can move the paper up a bit, if we can scroll down.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: The first page, only scroll it up, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, you can see in item 2 that --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Point 2, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You have it in your file. Could you find it, please, in the binder.

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR FILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I see now, 24 people were killed in the terrorist attacks and 31 wounded.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And what period does this summary refer to?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR FILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: 24 hours, it's a daily report.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And did the Pristina SUP deliver such information to the Pristina SUP?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR FILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Pristina SUP and all the secretariats delivered this information, and then it was compiled at the staff level, put together, for the needs of informing the ministry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Sorry, the sender of this information is which organizational unit?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The MUP staff in Pristina.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: That's the organization headed by Mr. Lukic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Now I understand. Thank you. Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] A correction, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: The body headed by Mr. Sreten Lukic, was it an organizational unit? Is the staff an organizational unit of the MUP?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR FILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we now look at page 2, we need paragraph 4.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Tell us what this paragraph describes and whether you're aware of this event or were you aware of it at the time it happened?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR FILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This paragraph describes a NATO attack, a projectile exploded in the village of Gornje Dobrevo, municipality of Kosovo Polje. It was near the main road Pec-Pristina, the main Pec-Pristina road, and six persons were killed including four women. The bodies were found near the missile crater.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: It says six persons here --

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR FILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, six persons.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: At the time did you know about this event?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR FILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we now have P1099, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: This overview of security-related events, again it's being sent by the MUP staff on the following day, the next 24 hours, that is. What does it say here, how many people were killed and wounded in terrorist attacks.

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR FILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It says that 20 people were killed and 16 wounded in terrorist attacks.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Do you remember who was among the wounded on that day?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR FILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that there was a terrorist attack on a police vehicle belonging to the SAJ commander, Zivko Trajkovic, on that day.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we look at the next page, last paragraph.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Do you see at the bottom of the page that the wounding of Zivko Trajkovic is reported?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR FILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, and his driver Radovan Aleksic was killed, whereas the following received serious injuries: Nikola Padovic and Velimir Popovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We now need page 3, paragraph 3.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: What was reported concerning an event in Kosovo Polje, what happened there and when?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR FILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the 27th of March, at around 1030, in Cara Dusana Street, near the bakery, the Metohija bakery owned by Idriz Hoxha, there was a terrorist attack on policemen carrying out their regular duties, and policemen Momcilo Simic and Radovan Pasic were seriously injured, both from the OUP in Kosovo Polje.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now we need page 4, paragraph 2.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: What was reported?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR FILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That on the 28th of March, at around 0800 hours on the main road of Nis, a Toyota car with a Belgrade licence plate was attacked, and in it were Russian journalists Aleksandar Pobrakov Andrejevic, Patnikov, Sergej Evgenovic, and their driver was Nenad Stojkovic from Zemun. On that occasion Stojkovic was killed, the driver was killed. The Russian journalists were not injured.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Well, let me ask you the following --

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Perhaps I should have risen earlier, but with this document, document P1100 and 6D614, the witness has really been reading entries from the documents and it hasn't really been indicated whether or not he's speaking about these things from his personal knowledge, having been reminded from the documents. He's just reading entries. So there's -- apart from that, there's no foundation for him to --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I'm exactly at the point what I'm intending to show the foundation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Please continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It says here, Mr. Filic, that it happened on the Pristina-Nis road. Where is that in relation to the town of Pristina?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR FILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's just as you leave Pristina in the direction of Nis near the Vranjevac neighbourhood.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: After this terrorist attack where did the terrorists attack refuge?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR FILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, most probably these terrorists took refuge in the town itself in the Vranjevac neighbourhood.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Do you know that after this attack an attempt was made to arrest the terrorists?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR FILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: More than once --

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Again, that is just leading.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Leading question, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I asked if he knows that somebody is arrested.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: That's a leading question. That's you giving him the answer. That's what a leading question is. It's a classic example. Move on to something else.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: How did the police react after this attack, your police from Pristina?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR FILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: After the attack the police made several attempts to arrest the terrorists who had attacked the Russian journalists in the area of Vranjevac neighbourhood, but they were unsuccessful because of the fierce resistance by the terrorist groups located in Vranjevac.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Do you recall how long this went on for?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR FILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Over the next two or three days there were several unsuccessful attempts to arrest the attackers.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: We now have a textbook example of what not to do followed by what ought to have been done. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Was there a constant air-raid warning in force in Pristina?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR FILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: From the beginning of the air-strikes on the 24th of March there was a constant air-raid alert. Many NATO planes carrying out their combat tasks in other areas flew over Pristina, and whenever the planes flew over from the direction of Macedonia and Albania, an air-raid warning was sounded so that while I was in Pristina we were constantly -- were constantly being warned of air-raids.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: During the night were there any orders to do something in relation to air-raids?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR FILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, since most of the air-strikes were during the nights, it was ordered to turn off electricity at 8.00 p.m. until 4.00 a.m. in the morning to make everything dark.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Did that have any adverse consequences?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR FILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course. These blackouts and the dark had certain adverse consequences because it suited all sorts of criminals, facilitating robberies, and other crimes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now call up back P1100, page 6, item 4.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: What date is this, what's the event? Item 4.

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR FILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's about the apprehension of perpetrators of an aggravated robbery in the area of SUP Pristina. In most cases in those initial days of the air-strikes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: How many people were apprehended?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR FILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: 21 persons were caught and arrested for having committed an aggravated robbery or an aggravated theft.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: On the English version there is not an item 4.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yeah, I can see that now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: And there is confusion clearly about these -- are these identical pages? It doesn't look like it.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: But number 5 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Is --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: -- in English is actually 4 in Serbian.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Ah, yes. Thank you. There are two number 6s.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Okay. That clarifies it. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now have 1099, P1099, page 5.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Page 5, look at number 5, the first paragraph, that's the next day for SUP Pristina. How many people were arrested?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR FILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The next day as well, 22 persons were arrested for the crime of theft.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we now call up 6D623, item 7. This is a different document than the one I meant. 6D614, page 142, please. Page 142 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Which item?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Item 67. Now we have the right page.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] What is this item about, Mr. Filic?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR FILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's about the measures taken against members of the police who committed certain criminal offences during those days.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Was it the practice in SUP Pristina to arrest policemen found to have committed a crime?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR FILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it was the practice to arrest such policemen, and I remember in particular one case when the CO of a police station brought into the building where we were relocated a policeman who had stolen a vehicle from an Albanian, filled it with some goods, and tried to go to his hometown outside Kosovo. We arrested him and turned him over to operative workers for further processing. A case file was compiled and the case was turned over to an investigative judge.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: What is item 68?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR FILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That a member of the reserve police, a certain Milivoj Niksic, committed the crime of appropriation of various objects, and a criminal report was filed against him to the district public prosecutor's office.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Which segment of SUP Pristina dealt with crime?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR FILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In SUP Pristina, in any other secretariats, it was the crime police as an organizational unit of the secretariat.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Sometimes it sounds funny when we ask such questions of people of your profession, but what was the main task of that section?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR FILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, to suppress and prevent crime, to work on all cases of crimes committed, processing these cases, pending the day when they would be turned over to the public prosecutor's office.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: In the town of Pristina and on access roads, were there any check-points and whose check-points?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR FILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were check-points, and according to a certain instruction there should have been a greater number of combined check-points manned by the police and the army. I know about one that worked all the time in Laplje Selo, that is on the Pristina-Urosevac road. I used that road a lot, so I know, and I believe on other access roads to Pristina there existed similar check-points.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: In addition to the army and the police, who else worked at such check-points seizing various goods?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR FILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The financial police, market inspections, they got involved in certain cases when certain kinds of commodities and goods were transported.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, I would like to ask this witness something in relation to two protected witnesses previously, Prosecution protected witnesses. So I cannot address their pseudonyms, otherwise they wouldn't know who I am talking about. So I would kindly ask to go to the private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: You're saying you need to use the actual names of the witnesses, is that --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Otherwise I can address whether they reported something or not, I cannot ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: We shall go into private session. If it turns out to be unnecessary, then we can undo that.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we are in open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: If a crime is not reported, can any steps be taken?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR FILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In serious cases like rape, we could act if we got information from other sources, but if the injured party does not turn up and we don't get any information from other sources then it's not possible to take any steps.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I'd like to ask you something now about the MUP staff. Are you able to tell us to what extent SUP Pristina depended on the MUP staff in Kosovo and Metohija in its operation?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR FILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: SUP Pristina was an organizational unit of the ministry directly linked up the chain of command to the public security sector, and it did not depend in its regular work on the MUP staff which was located in Pristina.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Was the MUP staff able to be any kind of equivalent to the provincial secretariat of internal affairs that you described?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR FILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it could not be a counter-part in any way in terms of strength or the function that the provincial secretariat had while it existed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And since when was the MUP staff in Pristina in existence?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR FILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe it was first set up sometime in mid-1990 when policemen and employees of the secretariat started leaving the service en masse.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Where were they located, the members of the staff, in 1990 and 1991?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR FILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the SUP Pristina building, on the second floor, they occupied a number of offices.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Who out of the SUP of Pristina was located close to those offices?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR FILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The office of the chief of SUP Pristina was close to their offices.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Did you go to the office of the chief and how often?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR FILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was in the building very often and I frequently visited the office of the chief because we had regular cooperation in our daily work.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Were you a member of the staff in 1998 or 1999?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR FILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was not.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Did you attend the meetings held at the MUP staff?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR FILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did attend a number of meetings held at the MUP staff, those meetings that were called for the expanded composition of the Kosovo leadership and 7 that were attended by the minister or some other officials from the Ministry.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We heard that you were the chief of SUP Urosevac?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR FILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: During your tenure as SUP Urosevac chief, were you invited to those meetings of the staff as a member of the staff?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR FILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was invited to provide analysis and briefing to the staff occasionally.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: When you took over as chief of SUP Urosevac, did anyone tell you that you were a member of the expanded MUP staff?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR FILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, nobody told me any such thing.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Did you ever get a written decision to that effect?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR FILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Your appointment as the chief of the Urosevac SUP, did it mention any such thing?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR FILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, that appointment, there was no mention of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Did you receive a decision on the forming of the staff ever?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR FILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Did you know at the time that in the decision on the formation of the staff it's -- it is stated that you as the chief of the SUP are a member of the expanded staff?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR FILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not familiar with that. I just said that I never received it, and in my appointment as the chief there was no mention of it. I was never notified of any such thing.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: At that time did you have any knowledge that David Gajic was a member of the staff?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR FILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I had no such knowledge.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Did you have knowledge that Milos Vilotic was a member of the staff?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR FILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Milos Vilotic enjoyed the same status as Gajic, and I didn't know he was a member of any -- such a staff either.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Did you have any knowledge of Milorad Ulemek being a member of the staff?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR FILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Did you have any knowledge that Zivko Trajkovic was a member of the staff?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR FILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The same answer stands, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: The people we mentioned for whom you said you didn't know were members of the staff, did you ever see them at the SUP in Pristina?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR FILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I saw my colleagues from the State Security Service, and they would often be at the local mess where they had lunch. I saw Vilotic and others who also worked for the centre -- security centre in Pristina. As for Trajkovic and Lukovic, I don't remember seeing them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Sorry, just one moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Who is Lukovic?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Could you please tell Their Honours who is Lukovic.

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR FILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Milorad Lukovic was the commander of the special operations unit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Did he go under any other name or nickname?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR FILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: His nickname was Legija.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: What part of the MUP did he belong to?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR FILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: To the state security sector.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Do you know at what level there was cooperation between the secretariat of the interior and the Army of Yugoslavia in Pristina?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR FILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In Pristina, while I was there until the 15th of April, as far as I know, that cooperation went on at the level of the commander of the 124th Intervention Brigade, Mr. Brakovic, and the commander of the Pristina brigade of the VJ, Mr. Mladen Cirkovic. It is possible that the traffic police chief, Mr. Vujosevic, cooperated with them since his men manned the check-points. There may have been some cooperation with certain units there.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: At what level was there the cooperation of the SUP and the VJ in Urosevac?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR FILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In Urosevac, the PJP commander -- company commander Lecic cooperated with the deputy commander of the brigade, Colonel Kolundzija.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: While you were in the area of Urosevac, was there a single independent PJP company -- Urosevac company unit executed --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction: Was there a single action carried out by the PJP company of Urosevac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Did you ever see Arkan's guards at the hotel of --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter didn't hear the name of the hotel.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I never saw them at the hotel. When preparing for my testimony here, I read some statements made by members of the KVM who said that it was so, but I believe it probably wasn't so, it wouldn't have been possible.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, the interpreter did not hear which hotel you were referring to.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Grand.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The Grand.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Did you ever find out whether there were any Arkan's units in Kosovo Polje?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR FILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. In Kosovo Polje there was a temporary base after their facility had been destroyed of the special anti-terrorist unit in the Masinopromet company in Kosovo Polje. Maybe someone took them for another unit, but only that unit was located there.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: What is the abbreviation of that unit?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR FILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The SAJ.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: In 1998 and 1999 or before or later, did you hear of the existence of a plan of organized moving out of Kosovar Albanians from Kosovo and Metohija created by someone in Serbia or Yugoslavia?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR FILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not hear of the existence of such a plan.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Within your service was there insistence placed on the protection of civilians?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR FILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Within our service we always insisted on protecting civilians at all meetings we held, together with the leadership and officials at the level of Kosovo. We always insisted on the importance of protecting civilians and providing assistance within the ability that we had.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Did you have any operational knowledge as to why civilians there were leaving?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR FILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: According to our operational information, they were leaving due to the fear of NATO bombardment and mutual clashes of members of KLA and security forces of Yugoslavia. There was also -- there were also orders on the part of the KLA leadership for them to leave. Reading certain documents, preparing myself for the testimony, I came across a document in which Mr. Merovci, who is Ibrahim Rugova's right hand, whereby he says that there were columns of vehicles leaving for Macedonia at Djeneral Jankovic between the 19th and the 20th of that month, right after the KVM had left. People started leaving Kosovo in columns. Then at Vranjevac, there were clashes between KLA members who had set camp there with the security forces trying to apprehend the suspected terrorists who had attacked the vehicle with Russian journalists. That could have been one of the reasons why people were pulling out of the area.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: What is the document you're referring to? Mr. Filic, what is the document that you're referring to?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It is a document concerning the moving out of Albanians from the area. I don't have it -- I don't have a specific document, but the question was whether there was a plan in existence of organized moving out.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: No, the question was whether you had operational knowledge as to why civilians were leaving, and you said that in --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Why they were leaving, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: And you said that in preparing for your testimony you came across a document in which Merovci --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It is Merovci's statement. He was Ibrahim Rugova's right hand --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Yeah, yeah, but you mean --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] He gave it to the investigators.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: His statement to investigators. How did you read that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I came across that statement when I was preparing myself for this testimony. It was with the other documents I was given.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: What was hit in Pristina at the outset of the air-strikes?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR FILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: During the first night of bombardment, the SAJ facility was targeted as well as the youth settlement buildings which used to house the units of the combined forces of the police. The airport was targeted, the barracks of the VJ, as well as the customs and roads administration. Certain buildings at Belacevac were targeted which used to house certain military units. There were explosions in that area. In the course of the next few days, the following few days, there were other buildings targeted, such as the SUP of Pristina, the postal office building, the VJ facility at Lukare and at Grmija, the Jugopetrol company warehouse was hit on that occasion together with a cemetery nearby. Then the Ina warehouse at Devet Jugovica, the bus station there. When I was still in Pristina our temporary residence was at Ibra Lepensa [phoen] building in the so-called Kicma settlement. A rocket landed killing an Albanian child who was in an apartment. A rocket landed at the outskirts of Pristina whereby a vehicle was killed with four people in it. Many other buildings were targeted as well in the area of Pristina and Pristina SUP.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: What about the central part of the city?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR FILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I mentioned that part as well. The Kicma settlement, and there was that child that was killed in an apartment block.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: After the air-strikes began, how did you communicate, how did you receive and send reports?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR FILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Our communication with Pristina and the ministry was done by couriers, between them and the SUP. When the secretariat and postal office were hit, after that there was no possibility for regular communication. We could only communicate by radio devices within smaller units and to a very limited extent because their communication could be detected and locations targeted.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Sorry, Your Honour, I have to ask you to go to the private session for another minute or two. Again, the Albanian citizen.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Very well. We shall go into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we're in open session.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we just have in e-court Exhibit P1100, page 3, page 3.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Can you see this paragraph which begins: "On the 27th of March ..." It's the fourth paragraph on the page.

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR FILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In Kosovo Polje?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes. What is this about?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR FILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's about a terrorist attack in which Dragan Stankovic, a policeman, was killed and a number of reserve policemen were injured.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: But what time of day was it?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR FILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At 0030 hours.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I don't want to put a leading question. What form of terrorism is this?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR FILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, on a freight train as far as I can see. It was an attack on a freight train.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Was it in a town?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR FILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, in the town of Kosovo Polje.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: So it's not really legible. It's a freight vehicle, not a freight train. Thank you, Mr. Filic. Those are all the questions I had for you.

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR FILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You're welcome.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Stamp, the point that you raised about the absence of evidence of the witness's own personal knowledge of the events in P1099, P1100, and 6D614, Mr. Lukic indicated he was about to address it but he hasn't addressed the point at all. There was at least one event in which it was plain that the witness was speaking from some personal knowledge, but I think we have to bear in mind also that he's the deputy chief of the SUP for that area dealing with these cases. And when we come to evaluate evidence of a hearsay nature such as this, then obviously we will look at the whole circumstances and decide what to make of it. We've also been told by the Lukic Defence that there will be a witness who is going to deal with this -- certainly the Exhibit 6D614. I don't know about the other two, but I wouldn't imagine the other two because they're internal reports coming -- dealing with the affairs in the Pristina area. So I think we would see what you said as a comment and indeed a warning comment to Mr. Lukic about the arguments that might be advanced later in the absence of personal knowledge.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Yes, indeed. Very well, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Petrovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Filic, my name is Vladimir Petrovic, and on behalf of the Defence of Nikola Sainovic I'll be putting only a few questions to you. Today you mentioned that at the time while you were working in Urosevac as a chief of the secretariat you attended some meetings which were held in Pristina in the MUP staff. I would like to know whether you recall attending a meeting held on the 7th of May, 1999.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And could we have in e-court P1996.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I did attend a meeting on the 7th of May, 1999.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Filic, do you recall whether that meeting was also attended by Nikola Sainovic?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR FILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Nikola Sainovic did attend that meeting, the deputy prime minister of the federal government, but he was there only at the beginning of the meeting and he left after the meeting had started.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Do you remember what he said on that occasion?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR FILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, he spoke about the current situation, the efforts being made by the state organs to regulate matters the way they should be regulated. Then he gave us encouragement. He said we were in a difficult situation, that we should hold on. It was a political sort of speech.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Please take a look at a part of this document, P1996.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In Serbian can we have the bottom of page 3 and the beginning of page 4, the top of page 4.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Filic, it will come up in a minute. The last paragraph on page 3 and the top of page 4. Please take a look. Have you seen page 3?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR FILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: And the top of page 4, please, in Serbian. What is this about, can you tell us?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR FILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, this is about a certain text which was published in the media and which contained state directives for the forthcoming tasks in the province. We received these texts even before Sainovic told us about them at that meeting.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Filic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have no further questions, Your Honours. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Cepic.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Filic, my name is Djuro Cepic. I appear for General Lazarevic. I will dwell a little bit on this same document. In your testimony you described relations with the Army of Yugoslavia. We're still referring to the meeting.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we have P1996 on the screen again, the one used by my colleague, and we're still referring to the same meeting. It's page 7 in the B/C/S version. In English I -- I'm not quite sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Well, here you have a record of what you said and here in the middle -- thank you. And midway through your intervention you say that relations with members of the Army of Yugoslavia are as they are in other SUPs, but when a military person is handed over for theft, do you see that? Do you know whether the persons you mentioned here were prosecuted by the judicial organs of the Army of Yugoslavia.

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR FILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: From the chief of the police department I learned that some persons who had been members of the reserve units of the army and who had been brought in were later seen again in their own units. And when I discussed this with the commander afterwards, I learned that they had, in fact, been prosecuted and that criminal reports had been filed by the appropriate organs, but that they remained part of their units until the end of the aggression and that then they would be tried subsequently. These were individual cases.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Filic, we heard testimony here from both Prosecution and Defence witnesses, and one Prosecution witness stated that when the aggression started at the exits from the town of Pristina there was barbed wire at the check-points and that movement of citizens was limited. Defence witnesses testifying here concerning the town of Pristina denied these allegations. I would like to know whether you can tell us something about this. Were there such measures, was barbed wire used?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR FILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I never saw barbed wire. I travelled between Pristina and Urosevac very often after the 15th of April, I -- and I never saw any barbed wire.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Was movement prohibited for any citizen?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR FILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no one was prohibited from moving around.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Filic.

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR FILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You're welcome.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours, I have no further questions for this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Filic, you will now be cross-examined by the Prosecutor, Mr. Stamp. Mr. Stamp.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Mr. Filic, while we are on this document, P1996, can I just ask you to look at what you said in respect to the VJ. And this is at page 7 of the B/C/S and that is page 9. You said that: "VJ officers were behaving rather incomprehensibly, and when a soldier is handed over to them for looting, they set him free with the excuse that 'these are our men.'" Is that what your investigations or your inquiries had revealed to you as the chief of SUP Urosevac?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR FILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This expression, referring to our people, it refers to a specific case we had. It was a dispute between a policeman and a group of soldiers. It doesn't refer to persons who were brought in for theft. If need be, I can describe briefly what this is about. When the commander told me, Filic, there are men, let them go, we'll see, measures will be taken. Can I explain what this was about?

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Please, go ahead.

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR FILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: A policeman from the police station was called by an acquaintance of his, an Albanian who was in Macedonia. He was invited to come and take a look at his house and see what state the house was in. The Albanian asked him to do this. It was a friend of his from Macedonia. When he came to that house he found a group of soldiers in that house who started arguing with him, asking him, What are you doing here. We are here now, and there was an argument, a heated discussion. And on his return the policeman informed his superiors of this. I informed Commander Jelacic, and he said, Well, let it go. They are men, maybe they were drunk. So this expression, our men, refers to that situation, not to situations where the military were brought in and later seen in their units. As their superiors explained, they had had criminal reports filed against them, they were being prosecuted, but they were not being held in detention.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: So when you told all the chiefs of SUPs and the assistant minister and General Lukic that our relation to the VJ are the same as those of the other SUPs and there were complaints from the other SUPs and that VJ officers behaved rather incomprehensibly when a soldier is handed over to them for looting they set him free with the excuse, these are our men, you were referring to that isolated incident that you just described?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR FILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Aleksic. Could you read the Serb. In English your answer does not make any sense. So could you read the Serb so we can see if there's some problem with the translation. Just read out what's written there on that passage that Mr. Stamp has been quoting to you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] "Relations with the Army of Yugoslavia, the same as in the case of other SUPs. The officers of the Army of Yugoslavia are behaving in a rather incomprehensible manner, and when a soldier is handed over to them for looting they set him free with the excuse that 'these are our men'" and so on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Now, in the example you gave, there was no person referred to by you as being arrested and handed over. Did that actually happen, that someone was caught for this particular event by the -- the event affecting the Macedonian -- or the Albanian, rather, who had been in Macedonia? Was someone caught and handed over to the army?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, no one was arrested. The policeman went to see that Albanian's house to see what the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: You've answered that. So what does this refer to, when a soldier is handed over to them for looting, who are you referring to in that statement?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Specifically I did not participate in their arrest. I got this information from the superiors in the police, that some persons who had been brought in were later seen in their units. It was the practice to detain those people, if they were civilians.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: But a moment ago you told us that's not what this was referring to.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I said that this expression, "these are our men," does not refer to them. That was the expression my commander used about those soldiers who argued with the policeman when he went to visit that Albanian's house, not referring to the soldiers handed over for looting but the person taking the minutes mixed this up.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Stamp.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: You spoke --

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: And if I could move on with your leave, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: You spoke that the media centre was based in the Grand Hotel Pristina -- or you said that.

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR FILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not on the ground floor, it was on the first floor in the Hotel Grand. He was upstairs on the first floor.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Are you aware of security-related activities that were carried on in the basement of the Grand Hotel?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR FILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not aware of that. I'm not aware of any activities in the basement of the Grand Hotel.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Did you have an office at the media centre?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR FILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no. I never had an office there.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Your Honours, I wonder if this is a convenient time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Stamp. Mr. Filic, we have to have a break at this stage, that will be for half an hour. Could you meanwhile please leave the courtroom with the usher.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: We shall resume at 11.15.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Stamp.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: You spent a significant amount of time during your testimony in chief discussing the MUP staff plan for 1999, the Pristina staff plan of 1999, that's P1074. Now, do these yearly plans that are -- that each SUP is obliged to prepare normally cover --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Sorry. It's not MUP staff plan.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: I think I corrected myself, didn't I?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: It was corrected to Pristina staff plan. It's the Pristina SUP plan that we're talking about.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: The work-plan for the SUP Pristina of 1999. That plan covered the routine operational matters of the SUP; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR FILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The annual work-plan of the secretariat did not cover routine but regular work within the secretariat that had to be done within the year.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Very well --

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR FILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: And that covered work that remained unfinished in the previous year, as we had seen in a number of examples.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Thank you. Did it cover major anti-terrorist operations in which large units of the MUP, for example, the PJP, would be engaged?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR FILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no, it did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: You also made a point that among other things it covered training of MUP members and that training was within the regular system of training within the MUP. Is it not true that in some areas when it came to complex security-related police work, the MUP staff or members of the MUP staff were involved in training policemen in the various SUPs in Kosovo?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR FILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At the ministry it was long-standing practice that every year from the level of the ministry plans for advanced training and education of policemen and other authorised officers be issued, and that covered certain topics related to regular activities, topics regarding changing legislation, et cetera. That was one segment. And another segment covered, for instance, the training of PJP, the reserve force, et cetera. All that came within regular training, not specifically linked to anti-terrorist actions.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Thank you. But was the MUP staff sometimes involved in training, particularly when it was linked to complex security operations or anti-terrorist operations?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR FILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: One of the members of the staff was responsible for assisting in the training of PJP. He also participated in organizing and performing the training of operative pursuit groups because he was specialised in that area, he was supposed to help the members of the secretariat in that training.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Who was that?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR FILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: To the best of my knowledge, it was Goran Radosavljevic as a member of the staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Could we bring up P3120.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Did Mr. Adamovic, I've forgotten his rank just now, but was he also a member of the MUP staff that was involved in training police personnel?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR FILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Adamovic was a member of the MUP staff until the bombing of the SUP Pristina building when he was injured, and then he was withdrawn from the staff. His responsibility had been to coordinate regular work of the police within the staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: What do you mean when you say it was to coordinate regular work of the police within the staff?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR FILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I mean to say that along the line that goes towards secretariat he extended all sorts of assistance, logistical, professional, specialised when the secretariats asked for it or when such a need was demonstrated.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: We have before us the minutes of the MUP staff meeting for July 1998, that is P3120. And if we could move to page 2 of the -- of both the English and the B/C/S. We see a description of the meeting, it was held at the premises of the Pristina SUP and it is dealing with the situation on the ground. And if we look at the other page we could see the attendees, and you are one of those attendees, I think you see that.

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR FILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: You attended in what capacity?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR FILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot remember exactly in which capacity, but I was not a member of the staff. It's possible I was invited as a spokesman. I really don't know exactly in what capacity, plus not all the members of the MUP were here. This was some sort of narrow composition. The meeting was led by Mijatovic and it was attended by a few people, probably about some sort of agreement.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: I think you had said earlier that you were or you only attended meetings of the staff in its expanded composition, but you will agree with me --

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR FILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: But this is not such a meeting. This is what you describe as a narrow composition of members.

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR FILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, if we look further below, the minutes say that I said that Bisercic would be coming early in the morning. They had probably invited me to help them about the engagement of some SUP members to do some work related to the staff. I think I say down below that Miroslav Bisercic would attend, it was an analyst who was supposed to help the staff in aggregating the information because there's Milorad Rajicic, Dobrasin Krdzic, Rasko Milenkovic, all of these are members of SUP Pristina, they were not members of the MUP staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: So it was probably that you were there in order to assist in engaging MUP staff -- sorry, in engaging SUP staff for work on behalf of the ministry staff?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR FILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Engaging certain employees of the secretariat, not the whole staff of the SUP.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Would employees of the secretariat frequently be engaged to carry out engagements or carry out work on behalf of the MUP staff?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR FILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, some did, like Milorad Rajicic, who was in charge of general affairs; Dobrasin Krdzic, who was a doctor; Rasko Milenkovic, who was chief of the analysis section. All of those being logistical services of the secretariat that catered to the staff in certain situations.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: If you look at the minutes here we see that Dusko Adamovic is discussing training and he says that training should be carried out in the barracks. Can you read for me just for the translation what he says about training.

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR FILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Dusko Adamovic: "It had been planned that Vukovic should" --

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: I'm sorry --

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR FILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- "deliver BRDs today and tomorrow and the training would be in barracks" --

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: What are BRDs?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR FILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Those are armoured vehicles that were received at that time for the requirements of the PJP, they were received from the Army of Yugoslavia. And Vukovic was the commander of that mechanised unit within the PJP. He was the commanding officer of that unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: So this training was organized by the MUP staff?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR FILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This discussion about training, but Adamovic says that it had been planned that Vukovic as the CO of that armoured mechanised unit should perform the training within the perimeter of the barracks.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Yes. And now that you see the document the question is this: From your memory did the plan to deliver these vehicles to MUP Pristina and to train PJP members in their use was something that was undertaken by the MUP staff?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR FILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know who decided that.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: While you were in Pristina SUP, did you meet with General Lukic?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR FILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I saw him at the staff, yes. I used to encounter him. The chief's office was on the same floor as his. Of course I ran into him from time to time.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: What was his role as commander of the MUP staff as far as you understood it?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR FILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, to my understanding he was a leader of a sort of forward working body of the ministry that was supposed to help the SUPs in Kosovo and Metohija in some situations that were complicated security-wise. He was supposed to monitor the situation in the area of the province, to summarize the outcomes of all these events and incidents, and of course it was convenient for the minister to have such a body and to have on his desk every morning aggregated information, summaries of all security-related incidents in that crisis area rather than receiving seven different papers from secretariats in Kosovo.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: I think you said that you never saw any of the documents that set up the staff or that designated the role of the staff. Is my memory correct?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR FILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have never seen the decision to set up the staff. Nobody ever informed me of it.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Well, you have just described what you thought was General Lukic's role as chief of the staff. How did you arrive at that understanding of his role?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR FILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I had worked for years in SUP Pristina and I know what the role of the staffs was since they started to operate. In hierarchy they were not superior to secretariats, they could not issue them orders, they could not assign employees, appoint them, or recall them or punish them. I think I described this in my prior testimony.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Let's look at one of the documents.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Could we look at P1505.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Before you move onto that can I be clear about one thing, the SUP Pristina, did you report daily direct to the ministry in Belgrade?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: So the reports that you say were coordinated by General Lukic were also being sent directly in any event to the ministry?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The reports that the staff aggregated for all secretariats from Kosovo went up to the minister, in that aggregated form.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: But you've just told me that also SUP Pristina reported directly to the ministry in Belgrade.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, but about the events in the area of SUP Pristina.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: So -- so your report was also sent to General Lukic so that he could combine it, the information in it, with the information in reports from the other six SUPs and submit a combined report to the ministry also; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Correct. The daily report from SUP Pristina went on parallel tracks to the ministry and to the staff. It went to the staff so that it can be combined together with all the other reports from other secretariats, and it went to the MUP as part of regular reporting.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Stamp.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: This is a decision of the minister, Vlajko Stojiljkovic, on the 16th of June, 1998. Are you saying that you have not seen this decision before, this document before?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR FILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have not.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Were you not shown this document during preparation for testimony?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR FILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no, I have not seen this document before.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: It says at paragraph 2 that: "The staff is tasked with planning, organizing, and managing the activities and use of the organizational units of the ministry, both the sent and the attached units, and suppressing terrorism in Kosovo and Metohija. "Also, the staff is tasked with planning, organizing, directing, and coordinating the activities of the organizational units of the ministry in Kosovo and Metohija in carrying out complex security operations." I understand that you haven't seen this document, but is that, what you see there in paragraph 2, your understanding as to what the role of the staff was?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR FILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I don't know because I have not seen this document before. Why would it plan and organize anti-terrorist actions if such a plan had already been adopted at state level to suppress terrorism and perform anti-terrorist actions. What additional role could be played by the staff in planning anti-terrorist actions?

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: What plan had been adopted at state level that you speak of?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR FILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The plan that I mentioned before in my evidence. I said there was a plan to carry out anti-terrorist actions by the MUP units and units of the Army of Yugoslavia from June or July 1998.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: You see here immediately before item 2 it says that: "The expanded staff shall also include chiefs of the secretariats for internal affairs ..." You were never told that this body in its expanded composition would include the chiefs of the SUPs?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR FILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was not told. At that time I was deputy chief, but I don't know about this and I said in my prior evidence that even when I was appointed as chief nobody told me that I would be a member of the staff in its expanded composition.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Is that something that is regular or normal in your experience in the MUP, that formal, written orders of the minister would be ignored and not communicated to those who were to carry out the orders? Is that your experience?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR FILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's not true, that I don't feature in this document and nobody submitted or copied this document to me. I was not in possession of it and according to this document I was not a member of the staff. It was not the practice, generally speaking.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Well, let's look at P1811, this one is dated --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: According to the document you became a member of the staff because you became chief of SUP.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] As I said, that even when I was the head of SUP no one forwarded any such document of that nature advising me that I am being made a member of the expanded staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
