utterances.text: Let's look at P1811.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: This is a similar order and this one again is signed by the minister, but this is the 31st of May, 1999, by that time you were chief of SUP Urosevac. And this is effectively a renewal of the last order I just showed you, and here again it says in the first paragraph after the names are listed, so if the -- we could scroll down a little bit on the B/C/S copy and the English copy on e-court. "Chiefs of secretariats of the interior and of the RDB centres and departments in AP Kosovo and Metohija are hereby designated members of the staff in its expanded composition." Now, this is an order of the minister. Are you saying it was never communicated to you that you would be a member of the staff?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR FILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was never communicated to me. This was towards the end of the war and just before we pulled out. I never received such a document.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Well, I'd like to go back to that question I asked you. This again is an order duly made according to the law and the constitution by the minister. Have you in your experience had other situations where orders of this nature of the minister dealing with the -- a serious issue, counter-terrorism, is not communicated to those who were supposed to carry out the order? Have you ever experienced that in any other situation?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR FILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I never came across such a situation in my career.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: You said today that you were invited to meetings of the staff in its expanded composition. We see here in this document that as chief of the secretariat you were designated a member of the staff in its expanded composition.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Excuse me, Your Honour, I would like to have the reference for this that the witness said that he was called to the meetings of the staff in its expanded composition.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: At page 21, paragraph 7 of the transcript -- sorry, page 21, paragraph 7 of the transcript: "Q. Did you attend any meetings held at the staff? "A. I did attend a number of meetings held at the MUP staff, those meetings that were to have an expanded composition where some officials of the ministry were visiting."

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Yes, Witness, when you used the term "expanded composition" in your evidence, weren't you referring to the composition of the staff as designated by the minister in his order?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR FILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It may be a mistranslation. I said that I attended the meetings of the staff when the minister was in attendance and when there was an expanded number of officials attended, chiefs of OUPs attended some meetings, commanders of police stations, and so on and so forth. I didn't say the extended staff per se, but in its extended composition, greater numbers of officials, although they were not members of the staff. The minister simply wanted to have a working meeting with a greater number of officials in order to analysis the situation in the province.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Could I, since I remember now, request a re-translation of that passage, just those lines.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could someone please read it out in B/C/S and then we can interpret.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: In due course. I don't think --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Yeah, what is required is that we ask CLSS to listen to the B/C/S tape and provide a revised translation of page 21, lines 5 to 8 of the English transcript. Thank you. Mr. Stamp.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Didn't General Lukic issue tasks to the SUP chiefs?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR FILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't understand the question. What tasks?

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Any task at all having to do with their work. Do you know of General Lukic issuing any tasks to the SUP chiefs?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR FILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: During the war when I was the chief of Urosevac SUP, he issued tasks by way of instructional dispatches on how to behave towards civilians and what measures to take in order to protect them against crime perpetrators. There were some instructional dispatches of that nature having to do with coordination of tasks at hand rather than complete sets of tasks.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Well, let's look at P1989. This is the minutes of the meeting with senior police officials in Kosovo on the 4th of April, 1999. And if we could look at item 2 which is at page 3 of the B/C/S, also page 3 of the English, we see in the minutes: "Forthcoming tasks." And Sreten Lukic, the head of the ministry, speaks thereafter. Without us going back to the first page I'll just indicate to you that the -- this was a meeting that was attended by all the chiefs of secretariats, PJP departments, SAJ commanders, and the JSO command. And we see General Lukic here issuing tasks, and this goes well beyond dispatches to protect civilians. And the last task he issues, which is at page 4 of the English, is a directive to the secretariat chiefs and unit commanders that they must report to the staff. The document speaks for itself. What I'd like to ask you: Under what authority could General Lukic issue these tasks?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR FILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wasn't present at this meeting of the 4th of April. I wasn't the chief of SUP at that time. I cannot comment these tasks. We can see from the minutes that certain tasks were issued, though.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Very well. I understand you weren't the chief of the SUP, but you did attend some meetings as deputy even from 1998. Very well, may I then move on to ask you about P1996. I think this is one in which you were a member --

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR FILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: -- a member -- sorry, a chief of a SUP. P1996, the staff minutes of the 7th of May, 1999. Briefly, if we can confirm the date there on the first page, 7th of May, 1999. This is a meeting that Mr. Sainovic attended, and you see the meeting was chaired by General Lukic.

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR FILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: And I think you will recall that was a meeting that you attended; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR FILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: If we look at page 10 of the English document, which I think is page 9 of the B/C/S -- page 8 to 9 of the B/C/S, where it says: "The head of staff Major-General Sreten Lukic contributed to the discussion as follows ..." And he issues several instructions. Again, the document speaks for itself. The question is this: Weren't you obliged, weren't you obliged to carry out those instructions issued by General Lukic or were you free to disobey them at your will?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR FILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We were obliged, by all means, yes, to carry out all instructions pertaining to regular tasks. It is clearly stated here that all cases with grave circumstances and consequences must be processed legally. General Lukic as the head of the staff had the role of organizing such meetings whereby senior officials would attend as well. He would chair the session and participate in discussions as well as provide conclusions at the end of each meeting.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: And in addition to that, while we are on this document, is it correct that the SUP plans for anti-terrorist activity in the field had to be approved by the MUP staff Pristina?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR FILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: While I was the chief of the SUP, I didn't draft any anti-terrorist plans and I didn't send any to the head of staff for approval.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Well, I'm going to show you a passage and ask you the question again. If we look at page 11 of the English, which is page 9 of the B/C/S. Should I indicate before we get to page 11, if one looks at the bottom of page 10 we will see that this is the assistant minister Lieutenant-General Stevanovic, who is recorded as speaking at page 11.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Move on to page 11 now, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: And you will see he says: "After the end of some of the larger actions such as the 'Budakovo-Jezerce' one, each SUP will be expected to work independently in organizing anti-terrorist actions in their own areas. The plan must be approved by the staff and will be carried out with manoeuvre detachments." Now, this is at a meeting that you attended. Does that not remind you that the anti-terrorist plans that the individual SUPs might formulate had to be approved by the MUP staff in Pristina?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR FILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Here Assistant Minister Obrad Stevanovic participated in the discussion. He wanted to let the chiefs know that there will be no significant anti-terrorist actions in the future and that smaller-scale actions can be planned at the level of secretariats, that they can execute with their own forces. The assistant minister was in Pristina at the time and he could only address the MUP staff in Pristina, that he could include so that eventually he would be able to receive and review such plans. He was there with some other officials such as Vlastimir Djordjevic and others; however, in the area of Urosevac there was no need for me for any actions of that sort. I didn't plan any and I didn't send any such plans to the staff for approval.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Yeah, but we'll get to Urosevac shortly, but if you could return to my question. Don't you now remember that in making plans for anti-terrorist operations the SUP chiefs or the chiefs of the PJP detachments or units would have to submit them to the MUP staff for approval. Don't you recall that?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR FILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't. I didn't make such plans.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: The assistant minister is speaking of the Budakovo-Jezerce action. Where was this action?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR FILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Budakovo territorially speaking fell under Prizren SUP; Jezerce was under Urosevac SUP. It is the area of the mountains around Jezersko which fell under the competence of both SUPs, Urosevac and Prizren.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Weren't Urosevac PJP units involved in this action?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR FILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was a PJP company that participated in the action. There was a company from Urosevac and from Gnjilane. As for the Urosevac area, I am familiar with that and they acted accordingly to the joint plan that they were handed down from the 124th Brigade. We had no part to play in that as a secretariat.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: This PJP unit from your secretariat participated in the action and the extent of your knowledge is that they participated in the action. You don't know or you didn't see the plan as chief of the secretariat?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR FILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't see the plan of that action. It was a larger-scale action covering a large area, and the commander must have received his task for his axis from the 124th Brigade; however, I didn't see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: However, the role of the PJP units in that large operation, one that covered more than one SUP territory, was it not something that had to be approved by the MUP staff? Withdrawn. I'll put the question this way: Various PJP units from more than one SUP are involved in what you have described as a large action. Which MUP entity in Kosovo was responsible for coordinating and commanding them?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR FILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Except for the PJP units of the ministry, as far as I know, there were some VJ units participating as well. As to who had drafted this joint plan, I don't know. I suppose this was done in Pristina in coordination between the army and the police.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: So basically when General Stevanovic says that SUP plans must be approved by the staff, you have no experience of the ministry staff approving these plans?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR FILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't. I didn't draft such plans and I didn't send them for approval. I have no knowledge of that nature.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: There are two separate matters here. There are the smaller actions which this document said had to be approved by the staff. There's also reference to the larger actions and as an example Budakovo-Jezerce is given. You say that that involved a unit from Urosevac and you were asked the question: Which MUP entity was responsible for coordinating and commanding the PJP units involved in that? Now, what is the answer to that question?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know exactly what entity, someone from the MUP or the VJ. I wasn't privy to that. I know that in my area there were units from Urosevac and Gnjilane, but I wasn't privy to any action details and who chose the tasks, who planned it, and so on and so forth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Stamp.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: I'd like to show you another document to the same effect, this is P1993, the minutes of the MUP staff for the 11th of May, 1999.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: And again we have the assistant minister addressing a meeting and this is a meeting, if you look at the first page there without reading all the names, you see many of the leaders of the MUP staff as well as the unit commanders, various PJP unit commanders. And at page 13 of the English, which corresponds -- I'm afraid I don't have the reference in B/C/S here. I'll read what Lieutenant-General Stevanovic says at page 13 of the English, and this is following on from the previous meeting where he spoke about large operation and small operations. He says: "Now we have to organize smaller actions or plan -- conduct closely actions in minor positions. Every SUP and PJP will establish a priority list of anti-terrorist actions with detailed plans which will be approved by the staff." Now, is what the assistant minister is recorded here as saying meaningless or don't you now recall that the SUPs had to submit their plans to the ministry staff Pristina for approval?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR FILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Probably if secretariats had such activities in their areas they would have to deliver that to the assistant minister for approval, but I did not have such situations in my SUP area.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Stamp, this document appears to have only nine pages in English. Can we clarify what you're actually referring to?

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Page 13 in the English and we have P1993.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: I think the problem is that I have a different translation than the one in e-court. It is possible that the translation in e-court was at some point in time substituted.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: And that is at page 7 in e-court.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Let's have page 7 then on the screen.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Which is page 6 in B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Filic, it's been pointed out to you that this document obliges every SUP to establish a priority list of anti-terrorist actions with detailed plans. You're saying you don't remember this requirement; is that your position?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] At this meeting, Mr. President, I did not attend. This was a meeting with the -- with the senior officers of the police units. I did not have a PJP detachment on my territory which was sent from elsewhere.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: That's not what we're looking at, Mr. Filic. We're looking at a provision that says: "Every SUP ... will establish a priority list of anti-terrorist actions with detailed plans which will be approved by the" MUP. Now, you're saying that that requirement was never communicated to you; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, it was never communicated to me because my superior officer was not at that meeting. I wasn't there. There was not a single detachment on the territory of my secretariat. It was only those in whose areas there were such detachments who attended.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: So that you understand the reason that these questions are asked, this is one of a whole series of documents that we're seeing where your evidence is inconsistent with the document, and it's important that we're clear what is the actual situation in your knowledge when we try to see what these documents amount to and understand them. Mr. Stamp.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: And I refer to these documents also because we have had testimony before the Court that you were actually involved, personally involved, in making these plans and preparations. Do you know brigade Commander Jelic or did you know him in 1999?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR FILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: He was commander of the brigade whose territory corresponded to your SUP, the SUP that you were chief of, Urosevac; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR FILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: I think out of fairness that you should have an opportunity to comment on what you [sic] have said, and this is at transcript 19084. "Q. We were speaking about your meetings with the chief of the Urosevac SUP. You told us that the chief of the Urosevac SUP during the war was Mr. Janicevic, is that correct," and he said Janicevic was the chief. And he goes on to say that he was later replaced by Colonel Bozidar Filic, that's you. "Q. And you had interactions and meetings with both of these men? "A. Yes, in the period when they were chiefs I was in contact with them and attended meetings with them." Is it true that you attended meetings with Colonel Jelic?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR FILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would see Colonel Jelic at his command post quite often, but as to my participating in developing plans with him that's incorrect. I did not draw up any plans together with him for anti-terrorist actions.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Well, seeing him is one thing; meeting him is another. The question is: Did you have meetings with him during the war?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR FILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What sort of meetings? I don't understand. I couldn't hold working meetings on behalf of his command nor could he do so on behalf of the secretariat. I had working meetings with my superiors, he had working meetings with his. We met to exchange information, experiences, discuss problems, and so on.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: He said at transcript 18958 to 18959 that when he received a decision or an order from the command of the Pristina Corps, he would begin planning for the execution of the task. In the course of his planning he would carry out coordination with the chief of the SUP. Did you meet with him for the purpose of planning? Well, he's saying you met with him for the purpose of planning these operations. Is that not correct?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I have to -- I would object --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I think that it should be precisely put to the witness on which period of time Mr. Jelic referenced this part of his statement, whether it was with Mr. Janicevic or with Mr. Filic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Stamp.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: The evidence of the witness Jelic has to be taken like evidence in general in context. He was asked about meetings with the SUP chiefs, and he said that he met with both of them, first Janicevic and later when he was replaced by Bozidar Filic, he met with Filic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, but that page was --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, let Mr. Stamp finish, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: That page is approximately --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Just a moment. Yes, Mr. Stamp.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: So this is a matter of an interpretation of the evidence. The witness is clearly -- the witness Jelic is clearly stating that in coordinating and planning his operations he met with the chief of the SUP Urosevac.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: What day is that evidence?

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: This is the 26th of November, 19 -- sorry, 2007.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: No, it can't be the 26th of November if it's 18958. 25th -- 23rd perhaps?

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: I have the 26th here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: 18958 is on the 23rd if that's the page you're referring to.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: The 23rd ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Filic, do you -- Mr. Filic, do you understand English?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: All right. We have an issue to make a decision about here, and you should not hear the discussion. Would you take the earphones off, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I'll do that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, Mr. Lukic, what is it you wish to add?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Exactly what you added, Your Honour, it's -- it wasn't in the same context, it was the other day. And I think that Mr. Janicevic will come here and testify as well hopefully and --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: But I'm not adding anything. I'm just looking at the page that Mr. --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yeah, it shouldn't be put to this witness that he planned. It should be asked whether he planned or not because there were two SUP chiefs, and this gentleman spent only short period of time in that city or in that SUP.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: I take it what you're saying is that it's not clear with whom Jelic said he was having meetings.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Well, he spent more than one year in that area with Janicevic and only a few -- couple of days with this gentleman, so --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: But the position is not clear, is that it?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: All right. Now, let's go back.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And it should be maybe clarified which year not only which ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Stamp, the question can be put on the basis I think of what you say, that this is the evidence of the witness and then -- of Jelic, and then you can ask this witness did he have any such meetings with Jelic.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Indeed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: And I don't see anything wrong with that. So we can resume. Mr. Filic, we've dealt with that matter. We can resume the evidence now. Mr. Stamp.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Did you have any meetings with Colonel Jelic for the purpose of planning joint military action?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR FILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I did not, Mr. Prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Can I ask you then what did happen when you met Jelic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We spoke about current issues, about regular activities, others were present, other officers. I usually went to see him together with the chief of the police department or detachment. We never had any such meeting concerning planning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Can you give me a concrete example of what you actually discussed?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The situation in the town, the current situation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: That's meaningless to me, I'm afraid --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] About controlling the road leading to Skopje, where there were constant terrorist group activities and attacks on both military and civilian vehicles passing along that road.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: What would you discuss about it? You wouldn't presumably simply be exchanging or passing the time of day and saying how dreadful this all was. What would be the reason for you to discuss these things?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The general situation, Mr. President, the general situation. We had to meet to exchange information and so on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Why? For what purpose?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, there were joint activities --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: You've just told us --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] -- of the army and the MUP.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: You've just told us you didn't plan joint activities.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I didn't plan them, but such activities were being carried out in the area of Jezerska Planina, for example, the Jezerce mountains, where his units were there from the direction of Strbac, the military territorial detachment, so there was a necessity for us to meet.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: So you are discussing the joint actions that the MUP and the VJ are involved in; do I understand you correctly?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We discussed how the actions were proceeding, but I didn't participate in the planning of those actions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: You see, that takes me back to the same question: Why are you discussing how the actions are proceeding?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, because the action was being conducted on the territory of my secretariat, so of course I was interested to learn how the -- how it was coming along. I had to be informed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Why? I don't want to put words in your mouth. What -- what were you going to do -- what were you going to do with the information?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Because I was responsible for the territory of my secretariat, so I had to know what was going on on the territory. I don't know if I'm failing to understand your question, but ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Why does a man in charge of the territory want to know what's going on there? He wants to know for a purpose, what is the purpose? It's a simple question.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, I had to inform my superiors about all events on my territory.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: So you were a postbox, were you? This is a war that's going on at the time that we're talking about.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: And you're just finding out things so you can report them to somebody else; is that what you're telling us?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Basically, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: All right. Thank you. Mr. Stamp.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I didn't participate in the war actions.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: At least one of the PJP units that was subordinated to your SUP was involved in ongoing combat actions with Colonel Jelic's brigade; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR FILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't understand the question. What combat action? What specific action?

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Anti-terrorist actions.

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR FILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: During my stay in the territory of Urosevac, my company -- I beg your pardon? My PJP company participated in an anti-terrorist action in the area of Jezerska Planina or Jezerce mountains, which I've just mentioned, and units of the Army of Yugoslavia, the military territorial detachment also participated in that action.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: And those VJ units were commanded by Colonel Jelic, correct?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR FILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was the commander of the military territorial detachment to the best of my knowledge from the area, and he contacted the commander of the PJP company.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Didn't the military territorial detachment, wasn't it subordinated to the brigade, to Jelic's brigade?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR FILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: So when you met with Jelic, didn't you discuss with him what your PJP unit, those men that you were responsible for, were doing? Did you discuss with him what was the plan for your PJP unit in the activity that they were engaged in?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR FILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He didn't give me any details about the plans according to which the terrorist actions were conducted.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Could we have a look at P1976, order of the 15th of April, 1999, for routing and destroying the STS in the area of Jezerce.

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR FILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: And you will see it describes in the first paragraph the enemy and it speaks about the forces has increased -- that's: "STS forces have increased in the general area of Mount Jezersko, more precisely the areas of: Budakovo, Jezerce, Nerodimlje, Petrovo, and Plesina." Are all those areas within the area of your SUP?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR FILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Which ones are not?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR FILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't see the paragraph very well, but Budakovo was not. This document doesn't look all right.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Yes, we -- we'll get to that, but Jezerce, Nerodimlje, Petrovo, and Plesina are areas within your SUP zone, aren't they?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR FILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: And if we look at page 2 in the English, it corresponds to page 1, I think, in the B/C/S. It says: "The Pristina Corps with reinforcements and armed non-Siptar population of Kosovo and Metohija supports the MUP forces in routing and destroying the STS in the area of responsibility. "Task: Support MUP forces in blocking, routing, and destroying the STS in the general area of the villages of Jezerce and Budakovo." And on page 2 of the B/C/S, which is page 4 of the English, I just want to remind you, you will see a heading: "Readiness." Readiness, the 23rd of April, 1999, so this was while you were -- while you had been installed as chief of the SUP Urosevac for approximately a week. Weren't you aware of this operation? Is this the operation you were discussing earlier?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR FILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, that was the operation, yes, I knew it was going to be carried out on the territory of the secretariat, or rather, when the operation began I learned that it was being carried out because it was on the territory of the SUP of Urosevac. That's where it was carried out.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: So it indicates here that it began sometime around the 23rd of April, 1999, and the document is on the 15th of April, 1999. Weren't you aware of the plan for this operation?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR FILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, not until the operation had started. When my PJP company was engaged, the chief of the police department informed me that they had been engaged in the action.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: How many people were in your PJP company that was involved in this action?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR FILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The company had about 130 men.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Stamp, can you find a suitable place to interrupt, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. May I just ask one question before --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: The document that I just showed you, had you ever seen this document before, the document that's on the screen there?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR FILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. No, I hadn't seen it before.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Perhaps this is a convenient time, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Filic, we need to break again, this time for an hour. Could you again please leave the courtroom with the usher, and we shall resume at 1.45.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: --- Luncheon recess taken at 12.48 p.m.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Stamp.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Last you told me that you had never seen this order. This is an order which emanates from the Joint Command. Had you during 1998 or 1999 heard of a body called the Joint Command?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR FILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I heard of the term Joint Command much later during a proceedings against Milosevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Very well. Were the SUPs -- well, I think you said that the SUPs were required to report on a daily basis to the MUP staff.

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR FILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: And these reports would include information about crimes that were committed, that is, serious crimes that were committed within the area of the SUPs?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR FILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The same reports went to the ministry and to the staff in relation to all security events or events important for security which took place during any 24-hour period.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Do you recall that General Lukic made a specific order or issued a specific order that you should report in particular about criminal investigations?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR FILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember exactly, but there were instructions in place concerning these new types of crime which began occurring in the wartime conditions, and the request was to inform both the ministry and the staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Okay. During 1999 General Lukic was the most senior member of the MUP that was posted -- that had his office in Kosovo and Metohija, was he not?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR FILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, as the head of the staff; however, even more senior officials came during the war such as assistant minister, chiefs of sectors.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Yes, yes. We understand that. If -- or what would his responsibility be, that is, General Lukic's responsibility be should he become aware of police officers committing serious crimes like murder?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR FILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was under the competence of the secretariat in the field to undertake measures promptly against such policemen and to inform both the ministry and the staff. Mr. Lukic, in my understanding, did not have direct authority to take measures in such cases; it lay with the chiefs of secretariats and regional SUPs.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: But he didn't have direct authority to take the measures, but did he not have authority to direct that measures be taken and that reports about the measures taken be made to him?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR FILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Certainly. As I said before, there were instructional dispatches on the part of the staff stating that measures should be timely and that both the staff and the ministry need to be advised of the measures taken.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: If I could move to something else. During the course of 1999 you were both the MUP spokesman and deputy chief for Pristina. Were you in any of those capacities engaged in disarming or collecting weapons from members of the Kosovo Albanian population?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR FILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Towards the end of the anti-terrorist operations in 1998, or rather, towards the end of September that year, some measures were taken in order to collect the weapons that Albanians possessed illegally, specifically I participated in one of such actions in terms of distributing pamphlets that were thrown out of a helicopter. We were trying to invite Albanians to hand-over their illegal weapons and to return to their homes. We were trying to tell them that they can live freely and that should they surrender their weapons no legal measures would be taken against them. That was my particular role.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: And just about the same time in 1998, were RPOs created or set up and the personnel of those RPOs issued arms by the MUP?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR FILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Reserve police squads, to my knowledge, were created during July 1998 when there were large-scale terrorist actions, in particular in the area of Orahovac, whereby many Serbs were kidnapped from their villages around Orahovac. That is when RPOs began being formed.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: And they were formed, were they not, by an order or as a result of an order issued by General Lukic, do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR FILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The decision on the forming of RPOs, I didn't see that, but there was a dispatch in circulation after that sent by the staff to the secretariats with certain instructions on how to form those squads.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Well, perhaps you could identify for us.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Could we look at P2804. The next page in B/C/S, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Is that the dispatch issued by General Lukic and the MUP staff Kosovo for the organization of these reserve police units?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR FILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is the dispatch pertaining to reserve police squads.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Who armed them?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR FILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The reserve police squads were formed out of reserve members of the police and the VJ. The VJ members were armed by the military and the police members by the police.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: What type of weapons were they given?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR FILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mostly semi-automatic rifles and the odd automatic rifle here and there, but I don't know how many exactly. Mostly those were semi-automatic rifles.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: And they remained under the command of the SUPs I take it? At least those armed by the MUP.

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR FILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were organized in every village. Those squads did not have their facilities per se. People stayed at home and they were simply issued with weapons. In case of need or any attack by terrorists on the village, their task was to organize a defence and defend their homes. The most experienced reserve member locally would be designated the commander and he was supposed to take care of their discipline, conduct, et cetera.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: And they were trained as well by the MUP?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR FILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. Certain officers within the OUPs of the police were in charge within the SUPs to monitor the conduct of those members. I don't know exactly who trained them, though.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: But you will agree with me if we look at this document we see that General Lukic or the staff orders that they should carry through the combat training plan in accordance with the plan that has been delivered to them. And if we look at page 2 in the English we see further discussion of the training plan.

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR FILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: And it is --

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR FILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It says that there was an obligation to train them.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Yes. And there are various plans?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR FILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know about those plans. As I say, I wasn't privy to that since other people were in charge of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Can I call up P2803.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: And while it is coming up, can you recall how many of them there were in Pristina while you were there, how many members of these RPOs?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR FILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't tell you an exact figure, but approximately rather. Did you mean the number of members or squads?

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: How many members -- or perhaps we could look at the document, and -- this is a report of the 16th of February, 1999, by Captain Blagoje Pesic to the MUP staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: If we could move to page 2 of both documents.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: As I was saying, it's a report of the 16th of February, 1999, by Colonel Blagoje Pesic to the MUP staff. Who was Blagoje Pesic in 1999, 16th of February, 1999, what was his role? He was --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Just one thing, I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We don't have, I think, this document notified. That can be checked.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Stamp.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: I am in the process of checking. I believe it was -- ought to have been notified and I see we have P2804 and P2805. I probably made an error and put P2805 instead of P2803. Very well --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Just hold on a second. Mr. Lukic, can you cope with the matter or is it causing -- will it cause a particular problem?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I just wanted to notify Your Honours. My learned friend was sometimes lenient for our delays, so I wouldn't object strongly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: There you have it, Mr. Stamp. You can continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours. And thank you to learned counsel.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Yes. Who was Blagoje Pesic at that time?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR FILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Blagoje Pesic, captain, was an officer with the police department of the SUP in Pristina. He was in charge of police work in the department. In addition, once the squads had been formed, he was in charge of that as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: If we take a look at page 7 -- sorry, page 4 in the English, page 4 before page 7, please, which I think corresponds to 3 in the B/C/S -- pages 2 to 3 in the B/C/S. We should perhaps go to page 2 in the B/C/S. You see here that he says that there are 255 reserve police stations. Is that -- does that conform to your memory of how many there were in Kosovo at the time?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR FILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Approximately, given the number of Serb villages around Kosovo and those which were ethnically mixed, this figure strikes me as correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: And in Pristina where you were there were, if we look at the table --

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR FILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In Pristina --

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR FILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were 48, according to the table, Pesic's table.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: There were 48 present -- representatives of 48 were present and seven were absent.

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR FILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, seven.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: And do you see -- if we could go to page -- the next page in the B/C/S, do you see at item 6 it refers to Urosevac. Do you recall that there were approximately 39 of them in Urosevac?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR FILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Approximately, yes. The police officer mentioned processed the data -- well, I suppose.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: And if we could have a look at page 7 of the English. I think that is page 5 in the B/C/S, he has a breakdown of the weapons issued. Total is 64.080. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR FILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do, and right-hand table.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: And just from your memory, you recall that in your -- in Pristina SUP there were 5.313 weapons issued?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR FILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot comment this piece of information. The figure strikes me as too high, but I really can't say. In relation to the number of reserve police squads, this figure is disproportionate.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: How many men were normally in a squad?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Depending on the size of village, there were large villages like Gracanica and Lipljan, the figure there could reach as many as 100, but there were many smaller villages in which there would be 25 to 30 people who were armed by the ministry. According to this figure, each squad should have had at least 100 or more members.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Well, do you have any recollection as to how many sets were issued in Pristina while you were there, that is, up until the 15th of April?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR FILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't say. The person who drafted the report was in charge of it. This figure is just unrealistic to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: And you see at item 6 in the table the number of RPOs for Urosevac, it's represented here as 36 and there were 1.928 --

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR FILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: And nine.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: I'm sorry? I'm afraid I don't understand what you're referring to when you say "nine."

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR FILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't understand that.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Very well. Do the figures here that you see for Urosevac, 36 RPOs and 1.928 weapons sets issued, are they in accordance with your memory of the situation in Urosevac at the time?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Just one short intervention. Do you want him to take off his headphones?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Filic, could you again please remove the earphones briefly while we deal with this issue. Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: At that time he wasn't in Urosevac, so he cannot have any recollection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Stamp.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: The question -- I'm sorry, maybe I didn't phrase the question correctly. I'm just asking if he recollects whether or not while he was in Urosevac those figures reflect the situation there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: As long as you phrase it that way, it will be satisfactory because this predates his involvement in Urosevac and therefore the situation may or may not have been similar. Thank you for your patience again, Mr. Filic. Mr. Stamp.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: The figures there that you see for Urosevac at row 6, is that the situation that you recall in Urosevac at the time you were there?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR FILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In Urosevac SUP there was an officer by the name of Zivic from the department of the police who was in charge of it. I came there during the war, therefore I cannot be precise as to this is fully credible or not.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Okay. But without being precise does it approximate to the numbers in Urosevac during the time you were there in April and May 1999?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR FILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The number of sections is approximately correct. As for the number of weapons, I think it's a bit smaller.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Now, the -- these reserve police stations or reserve police units, were they available for engagement by the MUP staff from time to time?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR FILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know on which tasks the MUP staff could have engaged them. I told you they were at home in their own villages, they were not at all engaged in any assignments until the beginning of air-strikes when they were disbanded because members of the reserve force went to the MUP and members of the reserve army units went to the army. So they were not engaged in specific assignments until they were disbanded.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: You are saying they were disbanded on the 24th of March?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR FILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The 24th of March when the state of war was proclaimed. The members who had been armed by the MUP went to join the reserve police units. It happened in a similar way with the reserve army units. Maybe one or two units remained in the territory after all.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Maybe my understanding of what you are saying is -- or what you have said is not correct. I thought you were explaining to us just now that when you arrived in Urosevac, 15th of April, the number of units were approximately -- reserve police units were approximately the same as in the -- as in the table you were shown, but you are saying the weapons, the amount of weapons, were perhaps smaller?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR FILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Prosecutor, this table was made before the war in February.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: I know.

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR FILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When I went to Urosevac, these RPOs did not exist.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: So you are not telling us at all that when you went there the number of RPOs that I showed you, 36, was probably correct but your memory was that the number of weapons issued to them was less? That is not what you are saying?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR FILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You asked me whether it was the case, not whether it was the case when I went to Urosevac. Looking at the table and knowing the number of Serbian villages in Urosevac, the area, and the number of Serb population, I said that it was approximately correct but it doesn't mean that I found those RPOs when I came to Urosevac in the form in which they existed before.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: I see.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Can we look at P1993. MUP staff minutes for the 11th of May, 1999, and if we could look at the last page, last paragraph, immediately before where we see the meeting concluded.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Can you read the last sentence there, please.

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR FILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the last paragraph?

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Yes, the last sentence. I think this straddles the --

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR FILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Members of RPO may not wear police or army uniforms unless they have been mobilised and engaged in reserve units of the MUP or the VJ."

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: This is General Lukic speaking. So as far as General Lukic was concerned at that time, 11th of May, 1999, the RPOs and their membership still existed?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR FILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have said that a small number of them probably remained outside the reserve forces of the MUP and the army, so it's probably a reference to that small number that has not been mobilised into any units.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: How many RPOs remained at the time, at that time, when General Lukic made this statement, 11th of May, 1999?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR FILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know that, Mr. Prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: How many existed in Urosevac?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR FILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know that any remained. Maybe some remained in those Serbian villages that didn't go to join, but I wasn't aware that any RPOs existed in an organized manner.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: You will agree with me, will you, that those that existed after the 24th of March were available to be engaged by the MUP or by the VJ if necessary?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR FILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't quite understand the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: You are agreeing with me now that at least some RPOs existed after the 24th of March, and I'm asking whether or not you will agree with me that those which existed after the 24th of March were available to be used or to be engaged by the MUP if necessary, the MUP staff if necessary.

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR FILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: During the war they could be engaged within the framework of their mobilisational units, the MUP or the VJ. They could not be engaged as RPOs.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Can you go over the page in English, please, to see page 9. There's no reference anywhere else, is there, Mr. Stamp, to their weapons; the reference is simply to uniforms, is it?

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Indeed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Now, I would like to show you a couple documents quickly, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Could we look at P3121. Could we go to page 3 in both the English and the B/C/S, I think, just to identify the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: What we have here are the minutes of the meeting of the staff for the 28th of July, 1998. This is one that you attended if we look in the list of attendees at the top of this document. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR FILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: I want to ask you about your role as MUP spokesman, but before I do that may I just ask you to look at page 7 in the -- it's page 7 in the English of this document, which corresponds to page 6 in the B/C/S -- I'm sorry, to page 8 in the B/C/S e-court. It's marked page 6 at the top, but in e-court it's page 8. You see where Captain Pesic is speaking, at the bottom of page 7 in English, if we could scroll down, please. This is also Captain Pesic confirming the issuing of weapons to citizens. He says that: "Weapons have been issued to 54.60 -- excuse me. Weapons have been issued to 54.683 persons. The MUP of the Republic of Serbia issued 12.170 ... the VJ issued 34.716." And in the last line indicates that: "'When all is finished, about 60.000 persons will have been issued with weapons.'" Do you recall Captain Pesic stating that at the meeting?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR FILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's what the minutes say, but below that you read about the request to the minister to be supplied with that. He probably found this number questionable because you see the Minister Vlajko Stojiljkovic reading that from a report asks that this report be sent to him.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: So you are speculating when you say the minister found -- probably found it not credible, aren't you? You don't know that?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR FILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know that, but I can see what the minister says and I can read that he asks to be given a copy of that report.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Anyway, without going through all of this document, you will recall at that meeting your role as MUP spokesman was discussed, do you?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR FILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: If we look at page 6 in the English, which I think corresponds to page 7 in the B/C/S, we have you saying that: "'We have many press statements that are given by various bodies which are not true.'" And the minister says: "'Suppress that and give equal access to the media, to everybody. Doctors and nurses must not provide any information on our dead, injured, or wounded personnel before we do'" --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: It's page 5 in B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Sorry. It's page 7 in B/C/S --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: That may be in e-court, sorry, but it's --

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: In e-court, but it's marked as page 5.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: -- marked as page 5.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: When the minister tells you to suppress "that," can you tell us what he meant by that?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR FILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Some civilian agencies like presidents of municipalities, the SPS, Municipal Boards gave certain statements. So where I speak we read in my contribution that with regard to the civilian sector Zoran Andjelkovic, who was part of that civilian structure in the Executive Council and the provincial Executive Council was already being established to be headed by him.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: When he refers to Zoran Andjelkovic, Your Honours, that's on page 7.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: What's that got to do with the question?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, here below I see that Zoran Andjelkovic is to provide such statements and information regarding the situation described before, nurses and unauthorised personnel should not be able to give statements as they please.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Yes, what I was asking was what did the minister mean when he told you to suppress "that"?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Excuse me, Your Honour, maybe it's wrong translation. In B/C/S the minister didn't tell it to Mr. Filic --

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Well, let's ask him.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: He said --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Let's ask the witness to read it and then we know what it says. Could you read the first line, first part of the statement attributed to Mr. Stojiljkovic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] "Minister Vlajko Stojiljkovic: Things like that should be suppressed and equal access to the media should be given to everyone."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Exactly, should be.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: All right. Thank you. Mr. Stamp.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Well, when the minister told you that things like that should be suppressed, what did he mean -- what ...

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR FILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He probably meant to say that unauthorised people should not be making statements for the public any which way they like and whenever they please.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: In other words, he wanted to control the flow or he wanted you to control the flow of information to the public; is that what he was suggesting?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR FILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no, Mr. Prosecutor. My role as a spokesman was not to deal with anything but anti-terrorist activities and to take foreign correspondents out in the field where these activities were being carried out. It was not my role as spokesperson to either hand out or suppress information.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Very well. If we could look further on I think you have that page there in front of you in B/C/S, and it's page 7 in the English, next page in the English, we see that the minister says: "'The media centre in Pristina has damaged us a little. We shouldn't write and say 'armed Albanians' but 'terrorists,' that is, not armed Albanians but armed terrorists. Don't write in reports that we killed an Albanian, but a terrorist.'" And you said: "'Zoran Andjelkovic mostly gives information about events in Kosovo.'" And the minister said: "'We should give less information on wounded and dead Albanians.'" Was the minister instructing you as to how you should carry out your role as spokesman?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR FILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was his opinion that he was expressing. I don't particularly remember this, but he didn't generally give me any particular instructions because when representatives of the foreign media go out into the field they're able to see for themselves.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: He was just -- is that your answer, that he was just expressing an opinion? Is that why he told you that?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR FILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, that's probably his opinion since it's on the record.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Very well. That is your answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Could we look at another document, P3122.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: And if we could go to page 3 of both of them to identify what this document is. Minutes of a meeting of the ministry staff of the 2nd of December, 1998. Present were members of the staff, including General Lukic; all chiefs of the SUPs; and commanders of the detachments; as well as yourself, Colonel Bozidar Filic. You see that?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR FILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Do you recall that meeting?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR FILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot remember exactly, but I see from the paper that I attended. There were lots of these meetings, so I can't specifically recall this one, but I attended.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: And incidentally you are saying there were lots of meetings where all the SUP chiefs were required to attend; is that what you mean when you say there were lots of these meetings?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR FILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not chiefs of SUPs, but -- I was not as a member of the staff, I was there as the chief of SUP, a chief of SUP, but I probably attended in my role as spokesperson.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: But there were many of these meetings held by the ministry staff with the chiefs of the SUPs; is that your memory?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR FILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Meetings were held, not too many. It's mainly those that you have the minutes of.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Major-General Lukic it says here, the comments made at the meeting: "Stated that on the 27th of November, 1998, in Belgrade, a meeting at the Ministry of the Interior was held which was chaired by Minister Vlajko Stojiljkovic and it was attended by chiefs of departments of the public security and the DB, state security, assistant ministers, head of the MUP staff in Pristina, and Nikola Sainovic. The ... security situation in Kosovo was examined in the meeting, in which the duties and further engagement of members of the police in Kosovo were defined." Do you know from what General Lukic told you at that meeting or can you recall from what General Lukic told you at that meeting what was the role of General -- sorry, what was the role of Nikola Sainovic in a meeting with the heads of various police departments?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR FILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember, Mr. Prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Do you recall what decisions came out of that meeting that you were told about or you don't recall?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR FILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: From this meeting of the 2nd of December you mean?

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: No, the meeting that General Lukic is speaking about in which Mr. Sainovic is present with the heads of the MUP for Serbia.

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR FILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't recall. I don't know about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Okay. If we look at page 7 of this document, and page 7 in B/C/S is page 4. E-court page 6 but designated page 4 in B/C/S. Where you see General -- and this is General Lukic speaking, I think you can make that out on the B/C/S copy -- no, it's on the previous page in the B/C/S copy and the previous page in the English copy. I represent to you, sir, that this is General Lukic speaking, and he's recorded here that he issued tasks to the various participants of this meeting. And if we turn the page, if we move to the next page in both English and B/C/S, I'd like you to look at a couple of those tasks.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: We need to move to the next page in B/C/S and the next page in English.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: The last task that he issues is that by the 7th of December, 1998, you are to submit a plan for the prevention of terrorism, which in principle should contain, and he lists eight factors or eight elements. Do you recall General Lukic instructing the persons there to submit to him a plan?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR FILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember this, Mr. Prosecutor. I don't remember this part.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: I think if you look at item 6 one of the elements is the: "Security of facilities (in particular in the OUPs in Glogovac ..." Do you remember who was the chief of the OUP in Glogovac at that time?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR FILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The chief of the Glogovac OUP was Petar Damjanac at that time.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Filic.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Your Honours, I have nothing further for this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you. Questioned by the Court:

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Filic, you've told us that the PJP's principal commander in Kosovo was the commander of the 124th Intervention Brigade. To whom was he answerable?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR FILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The command of the 124th Brigade was the commander of that brigade. That brigade comprised members of the PJP company and the secretariat from the Kosovo area. So he was not the chief commander of all the PJP, but only of that brigade from the Kosovo area.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: So let me be clear then. The commander of the 124th Brigade was the chief commander of the PJP who were operating in Kosovo; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR FILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, not all the PJP who were operating in Kosovo, only of the 124th Brigade. That brigade --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: When he was on his PJP duties, to whom was he answerable?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR FILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: His superior was the commander of all the PJP, all the PJP detachments.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: And who was that?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR FILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When I was in the PJP and led the Kosovo PJP, it was General Obrad Stevanovic who was in charge of that and then later on he became the assistant minister, and whether as such he was in charge of the PJP I don't know exactly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: So your answer is that in 1999 -- 1998 and 1999 you do not know who was in charge of the PJP?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR FILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think it was General Obrad Stevanovic, but I know that officially he was the assistant minister.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Closed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We were in closed session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: We'll go into private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: (redacted) [Part of the confidentiality lifted by later order of the Chamber]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: You gave us a description of the -- a brief description of the role of Adamovic in the work of the MUP staff. Could you tell me again what the role of Adamovic was in the MUP staff?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR FILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the MUP staff, to the best of my knowledge from my contacts with them, the head of the staff, the chief of the staff, had assistants for police, crime prevention, border, foreign nationals, and traffic affairs, and he was the assistant of the Chief of Staff for police work. He dealt with the work of police stations and probably work on the ground.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Can you give me an example of the sort of thing he would do, a concrete example?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR FILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, in concrete terms, what could I say? It's possible that he provided assistance where the secretariats asked for it, to the police stations to put the police records in order, to put the files in order because the work was done according to the sector principle and he had quite a lot of experience in -- in organizing such activities. So when asked for assistance he could provide instruction.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: So were the secretariats not good at keeping records?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR FILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, perhaps in some secretariats in some police departments they needed some assistance in that respect. Where you asked me to be specific, concrete, I don't know what else I could say.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Any re-examination, Mr. Lukic?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Sorry, there was no need for private session beyond the reference -- just hold on a second until I give you a page. Yeah, and after 22.18. So, from 22.19 onwards should not have been in private session and we can now return to open session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we are back in open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] His Honour Judge Bonomy put a question to you, and that was to be my first question actually to you. To what line of work did Mr. Adamovic belong, what line of work did he belong to?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR FILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean in the ministry?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, in the ministry.

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR FILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, to the police administration in the ministry.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Is that the uniformed or the non-uniformed part?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR FILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's the uniformed part.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we now have in e-court P1989.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: These are minutes of a meeting held with the leading police employees, senior police officials in Kosovo and Metohija. First of all, did you attend this meeting?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR FILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now see page 3.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: At the bottom of the page under number 2 we see that Sreten Lukic, the chief of the -- the head of the staff took the floor, but we also see that General Obrad Stevanovic also attended. I would like to ask you whether Lieutenant-General Stevanovic could also issue tasks to the MUP units?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR FILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, certainly.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: In the second bullet point, the first, Sreten Lukic, head of staff of the ministry, and then the second bullet point: "The MUP carries out its tasks in time of war just as in peacetime, the perpetrators of crimes are treated the same as in peacetime ..." Is this something new, a new order, or is it simply updating something that is already a task of the SUP?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR FILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, this is nothing new. This is a regular, ongoing task, which is simply being updated, as you put it.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Third bullet point: "Functioning of all other services in security matters shall proceed as ordered by the secretariat and the secretariat chiefs are responsible for this." Did Sreten Lukic introduce this duty here for the first time?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR FILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Or was it a regular, ongoing task?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR FILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was a regular task, functioning of the secretariat.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And to whom were you responsible as chiefs of the secretariat, were -- you still weren't at that post but to whom were chiefs of the secretariats responsible?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR FILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: To the chief of the public security sector in the ministry.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: The last bullet point was read out to you: "Compulsory reporting of the chiefs of the secretariats and the commanders of the units to the staff." Are you aware that at that time, the 4th of April, 1999, the SUPs and OUPs were a target of NATO aviation --

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: That sounds like it's going to be a leading question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: If he knows.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: But you've given him the answer. It really -- you know, if he does or doesn't know is neither here nor there now. There's an invitation to answer the question in a particular way. It doesn't remove the nature or change the nature of the question that you put the words "do you know" in front of it.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Was a building hit at that time belonging to the Ministry of the Interior, up to that time?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR FILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Pristina SUP was targeted, the SUP building in which a brigade was billeted within the barracks. I think that buildings for accommodating people belonging to the secretariat were all targeted, as were the barracks.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Did Obrad Stevanovic have an address in Kosovo and Metohija outside the MUP staff?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR FILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think he did. He and Djordjevic stayed in the staff premises when they visited.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You were asked today on page 64, line 8, and by His Honour Judge Bonomy about your meetings with Lieutenant-General Jelic, the commander of the brigade that was deployed in your territory. And you were asked about the subject of your conversation with him. Forget planning now. Don't think about planning the action now. Did you send patrols out onto the ground usually?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR FILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What patrols do you mean, police patrols?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR FILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, certainly.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Did you discuss with him -- did you discuss with him anything about patrols?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR FILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We had a joint check-point on the road to Skopje with members of the military police.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Were there any movements of civilians?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR FILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When I left for Urosevac, those Albanians who had intended to leave had left already. There were no movements of civilians apart from movements from Gnjilane via Urosevac towards the border.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Remember, please, whether you discussed anything else with Jelic, nothing to do with planning.

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR FILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't remember. I think sometimes you can have a cup of coffee with someone and just talk without discussing anything in particular. I find it hard to remember now after ten years.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: What did you do after the operation was completed?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR FILIC [Resumed]
